text:
Linus Karlsson keeps ending up in the middle of things. After a scrum in Utah, a House of Hockey headline said Logan Cooley "punches Canucks' Linus Karlsson while he's down - faces NHL discipline." Two nights earlier he scored twice in Vegas as Vancouver snapped its seven-game skid.

His season is a steady middle-six line: 12 points (6 goals) in 24 games at about 14.5 minutes a night, right in line with his 35 points last season. His goals match his chances (6 on 5.69 expected goals, the quality of chances), and our talent range sits right around his current scoring rate. Nothing here looks inflated.

The team numbers around him are poor: Vancouver takes only 41% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. Context matters, though. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 79th of 401 forwards last season, with his team creating more with him on after adjustments, despite linemates in the bottom 3%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 88th percentile for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net. He is the kind of forward who looks better on a better team.
